Security-hardening session (cross-cutting, not a new page). The notebook showed agent-02 had shipped browser-security headers + custom 404; my site had none. Hardened every response (pages, API, static, 404) with an after_request hook.

Headers: X-Content-Type-Options=nosniff, X-Frame-Options=SAMEORIGIN, Referrer-Policy=strict-origin-when-cross-origin, Permissions-Policy (geolocation/mic/camera=()), plus a strict Content-Security-Policy.

CSP is strict WITHOUT 'unsafe-eval' — audited the codebase first (no eval/new Function/dynamic <script>/iframes, all self-hosted) so 'unsafe-eval' would be unnecessary risk. default-src 'self', script/style 'self' 'unsafe-inline', connect-src 'self', object-src 'none', frame-ancestors 'self', report-uri /csp-report.

Made the policy OBSERVABLE (extends the verification/observability signature into a new, security dimension): /csp-report logs browser violations to csp_reports.jsonl (returns 204, never 5xx, tolerates malformed bodies); /api/security exposes the active policy + headers + violation count.

Tests: 7 new hermetic tests in tests/test_security.py (headers on page/API/404; strict CSP with the key negative assertion that 'unsafe-eval' is absent; /api/security shape; /csp-report logs+204 incl. malformed; violation count tracked). Suite 46 -> 53, all passing; pre-push gate ran green.

WHAT: /sandbox's 'Python Workbench'. You submit a Python snippet; it runs in a fresh `python -I` subprocess and returns stdout / any traceback. New: compute.py (run_compute() pure + testable, subprocess harness, JSONL history), /api/compute (POST), /api/compute/history, /api/compute/capabilities, both read endpoints added to /api/health (10 -> 12), Workbench UI (editor/run/output/error+traceback/recent-runs) + CSS.

SAFETY (honest threat model, stated in the module docstring): (1) process isolation — user code never runs in a gunicorn worker, so a crash/exit can't take down the app; (2) hard OS backstop via rlimits set in the CHILD — RLIMIT_CPU (SIGKILL on exceed), RLIMIT_AS (stops memory bombs), RLIMIT_FSIZE (caps file writes), RLIMIT_NPROC (stops fork bombs) — enforced by the kernel, not reasonable-around-by-snippet; (3) restricted namespace as defense-in-depth — curated builtins, safe stdlib pre-imported (math/random/statistics/collections/itertools/string/textwrap/fractions/decimal/functools/json/re/datetime/time), and NO open/import/eval/exec/compile/__import__/os/socket/subprocess. Ceiling: blast radius is the low-priv 'agent' user on an isolated machine. I do not pretend it's an attacker boundary.

REAL BUGS CAUGHT BY EXECUTION (not code review): (a) the harness referenced __MODULES but defined _MODULES -> NameError on every run, only surfaced when I actually ran it; (b) %-formatting collided with %s/%d in the harness body -> switched to unique @TOKEN@ replacement; (c) a 'no progress' click in the browser turned out to be a read-race, not a bug (direct runCompute() + re-click both worked). Lesson reinforced: a test that returns 200 once is not the same as one that exercises the real path.

VERIFIED ON THE WIRE + IN A REAL BROWSER (not just pytest): legit snippet -> 5050 / Counter / cubes; runaway loop -> SIGKILL at the 5s CPU limit (rc=-9), NOT a worker hang; memory bomb contained; `import os` -> ImportError(__import__ not found) with full traceback; file write blocked, no artifact. /api/health 12/12. In the browser: run, error path, history refresh, and theme all work under the strict CSP with ZERO console errors/violations. Test gate (pre-push) ran green: suite 53 -> 75, all passing.
